Here is his reply: Modern model locomotives may have some lighting features that are dependent on components and wiring built into the factory-installed circuit board. candidates.title: Maersk cuts emergency surcharge from Indian Subcontinent to Latin America
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will reduce its Emergency Contingency Surcharge (ECS) on the B1S trade from the Indian Subcontinent to the West Coast of Latin America. The surcharge will decrease by US$500 across all listed container types from the Price Calculation Date of 10 October 2026. The revised charges cover shipments to the West Coast of South America, the Caribbean and Central America. The revised rates also apply to out-of-gauge (OOG), shipper-owned (SOC) and non-operating reefer (NOR) containers. Rates for 40-foot flat racks, open tops and NOR equipment will match those for 40-foot dry containers. Northwest India covers Mundra, Jawaharlal Nehru, Hazira and Pipavav. South and East India covers Ennore, Chennai, Kattupalli, Tuticorin, Visakhapatnam, Kolkata, Cochin, Mangalore and Haldia. The changes remain subject to applicable regulatory approvals and notice periods.

candidates.title: News photo: Soo Line 2-8-2 No. 1003’s fall run
candidates.excerpt: HARTFORD, Wis. — The early-autumn weather was perfect on Saturday, Sept. 26, as Soo Line Mikado No. 1003 rambled across Wisconsin farmland between Hartford and Burnett, Wis. Temperatures in the low 70s drew hundreds out to watch the 113-year-old 2-8-2 cross country roads and pass classic Midwestern farm scenes. Here, the locomotive and train skirt a field outside the tiny village of Iron Ridge, Wis. The train is on its return leg, eastbound, returning to Hartford after turning and taking on coal in Burnette. The excursion took place on Watco’s Wisconsin & Southern Railroad. No. 1003 is a relatively large Mikado, weighing in at 250 tons and producing 53,947 pounds starting tractive effort. It was a member of the Soo Line’s L-1 class, operating across all parts of the railroad’s system. No. 1003 ran for 46 years before being retired in 1959. Intermodal rail powers up with 7% gain for latest week
candidates.excerpt: Rail traffic on U.S. carriers came to 535,663 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.9% compared with the same week last year, according to Association of American Railroads data for the week ending Sept. 19. Total carloads reached 234,207 units, up 2.4%, while intermodal volume was 301,456 containers and trailers, better by 6.9% compared to 2025. Seven of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. candidates.excerpt: Texmaco Rail & Engineering rallies on Rs 131-crore order win Texmaco Rail & Engineering rose 5.07% to Rs 121.87 after the company announced orders worth a combined Rs 131.36 crore. The company received two domestic orders. Transport Corporation of India awarded a Rs 24.48-crore order for the manufacture, supply and commissioning of one rake of Type ACT-1 wagons along with one BVCM wagon. The order is to be executed within 16 weeks from the date of the letter of intent. Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing awarded a Rs 106.88-crore order for the manufacture and supply of four rakes of BFNS22.9 wagons along with four BVCM wagons. The order is to be completed by 26 May 2027. Texmaco Rail & Engineering is one of the promoters of Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing. The company said there is no conflict of interest and the transaction has been carried out on an arm's-length basis.
